items.question_text: You are managing Google Cloud infrastructure with Terraform. The Terraform configuration files are stored in a Git repository. You need to implement a solution that enables multiple team members to work on the Terraform configurations concurrently without conflicts and ensures that sensitive values are not persisted to local machines. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Configuring a Cloud Storage backend moves the Terraform state file to a remote, centralized location. This enables automatic state locking and concurrent access for multiple team members while preventing sensitive data from being persisted on local machines.

choices.text: Configure a local backend in Terraform, and deploy all changes by using a shared account on a bastion server.
Configure a Cloud Storage backend in Terraform.
Configure a local backend in Terraform, and store the state file in a Git repository.
Configure a local backend in Terraform, and manually share the Terraform state file with team members after every change.

items.question_text: You work for a large company that recently acquired three smaller startups. All of the startups’ Google Cloud resources must be centrally managed under a single Google Cloud organization. However, each startup has its own budget and financial reporting structure. You need to ensure that each startup receives a separate monthly invoice for its Google Cloud consumption. What should you do?
items.solution_text: The requirement for central management under a single organization eliminates options involving multiple organizations (C and D). To generate separate monthly invoices, each startup must have its own Cloud Billing account, as a single billing account produces only one consolidated invoice regardless of folder structure (eliminating A). Therefore, creating folders within a single organization while assigning distinct billing accounts to each folder satisfies both the management and invoicing requirements.

choices.text: Create a Google Cloud organization with a folder for each startup. Share a single Cloud Billing account, and use the detailed billing export to allocate costs.
Create a Google Cloud organization with a folder for each startup. Configure each startup to have its own Cloud Billing account.
Create a Google Cloud organization for each startup. Configure each startup to have its own Cloud Billing account.
Create a Google Cloud organization for each startup. Share a single Cloud Billing account, and use the detailed billing export to allocate costs.

items.question_text: You are troubleshooting a complex application failure. You found several cryptic error messages containing no personally identifiable information (PII) in Cloud Logging that you do not recognize. You need to understand the meaning of these logs and determine what actions to take as quickly as possible. What should you do first?
items.solution_text:
The 'Explain this log entry' feature in Cloud Logging leverages Gemini to interpret cryptic logs and suggest remediation steps, directly addressing the need for speed and understanding.
This AI-assisted tool is specifically designed to help users decode unfamiliar error messages quickly without manual search or code inspection.

choices.text: Manually copy the error messages, and search for them in public forums and documentation.
Use Cloud Profiler to analyze the application’s performance during the time of the errors.
Use the “Explain this log entry” feature in Logs Explorer, and start a conversation with Gemini.
Search the application source code to determine the cause of the errors.

items.question_text: You are managing logging for your organization by aggregating logs into a centralized Google Cloud project. The aggregated logs come from two source projects: one for a frontend application and one for a backend application. You need to grant the frontend development team access to view all logs originating from the frontend project and only error-level logs from the backend project. The team must not be able to view any other logs. You want to follow the principle of least privilege and develop a cost-efficient solution. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Log Views are the most cost-efficient and precise mechanism for restricting access to specific subsets of logs without incurring additional storage or routing costs.
By granting the logging.viewAccessor role on a filtered view containing only frontend logs and backend ERROR logs, you adhere to the principle of least privilege by ensuring users cannot see any other logs.

choices.text:
• In the centralized logging project, craft a query that combines all logs from the frontend project and error-level logs from the backend project, and grant the logging.viewer IAM role.
• Save and share this query with the frontend team for them to use in the Logs Explorer.
• Request the frontend team not to use any other query.

• Create two separate log sinks in the centralized project.
• Configure one sink to route all frontend logs to a new, dedicated Cloud Storage bucket.
• Configure a second sink to route only the error-level logs from the backend project to that same bucket.
• Grant the frontend team read-only access to this bucket.

• Grant the frontend team the logging.viewer IAM role on both the frontend project and the backend project.
• Instruct the developers to use a specific filter in the Logs Explorer to find the logs they need.

• In the centralized logging project, create a log view on the bucket that contains the aggregated logs.
• Filter the view to include all logs from the frontend project and only logs with a severity level of ERROR from the backend project.
• Grant the frontend team the logging.viewAccessor IAM role on this specific view.

items.question_text: You are managing resources in a Google Cloud project. A new service account needs the ability to invoke a Cloud Run service. You need to gain the permissions to modify IAM policies for service accounts while adhering to the principle of least privilege. What should you do?
items.solution_text: The question requires modifying IAM policies specifically for service accounts while adhering to the principle of least privilege. The `roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin` role grants the necessary permissions to create, update, and manage service accounts and their associated IAM policies without providing broader administrative access to the entire project like the Editor or Owner roles would.

choices.text: Request the roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin role for your user account.
Request the roles/run.invoker role for your user account.
Request the Editor role for your user account.
Request the Owner role for your user account.
